name: browserkey
displayName: BrowserKey: AI API Key Exposure in Frontend Code Checker
description: Catches OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral and other AI provider API keys that end up in the browser: NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, REACT_APP_, EXPO_PUBLIC_, NUXT_PUBLIC_, GATSBY_ and SvelteKit/Astro PUBLIC_ variables holding AI keys, SDK clients created with dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true, server-only keys read in "use client" components, keys inlined by vite define, DefinePlugin or next.config env, and hardcoded keys in frontend code. Secrets are always masked, fully offline.

virtualWorkspaces.description: BrowserKey reads source, .env and build files from local disk.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Open a folder with a web or mobile frontend and BrowserKey checks whether any AI provider API key reaches the browser.
[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

No AI API key reaches the browser.
BrowserKey looks for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral and other AI keys in NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, REACT_APP_, EXPO_PUBLIC_, NUXT_PUBLIC_, GATSBY_ and PUBLIC_ variables, SDK clients with dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true, server-only keys read in client components, keys inlined by vite define, DefinePlugin or next.config env, and hardcoded keys in frontend files.
[Rescan Workspace](command:browserKey.rescan)

browserKey.enabled.description: Check whether AI provider API keys reach browser or app bundles.

BK001.description: Public-prefixed variable holds an AI provider key (.env, CI, Dockerfile, compose, nuxt runtimeConfig.public).

BK002.description: Public AI key variable read in client code.

BK003.description: SDK client created with dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true (default: error, information when the key comes from the user).

BK004.description: Server-only AI key read in a client-side file.

BK005.description: AI key inlined into the bundle by vite define, DefinePlugin, EnvironmentPlugin, next.config env or envPrefix.

BK006.description: Hardcoded AI provider key in frontend code.

browserKey.rules.markdownDescription: Severity per rule, or `off`, e.g. `{ "BK004": "information", "BK003": "warning" }`. Defaults: BK004 warning, all others error (BK003 is information when the key comes from a user-supplied field).

browserKey.extraPublicPrefixes.markdownDescription: Extra variable name prefixes that your build exposes to client code, e.g. `["STORYBOOK_", "APP_"]`. Built in: `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_`, `REACT_APP_`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_`, `NUXT_PUBLIC_`, `GATSBY_`, and `PUBLIC_` in SvelteKit and Astro projects. A Vite `envPrefix` or SvelteKit `publicPrefix` written as a string literal in the config file is picked up automatically.

browserKey.ignoreNames.markdownDescription: Regular expression for variable names that are never reported, e.g. `^NEXT_PUBLIC_.*_PROXY_KEY$` for a key to your own proxy. At most 200 characters. In an untrusted workspace only your user setting is used.

browserKey.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files scanned in the workspace (open files are always checked). Files over 1 MB are skipped.

browserKey.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns (workspace-relative) that are never scanned. `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build` and `vendor` are always excluded. In an untrusted workspace only your user setting is used.
